newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was uneven on light to moderate demand and offerings, USDA said.

Retail and HRI demand was generally light for immediate pre-holiday needs, while good interests on both immediate and forward needs was noted on rib cuts especially on the lighter weight cuts which was sharply higher for the week.

Chuck cut demand most of the week was fairly slow, but late in the trading period some improvement was noted, especially on the Choice cuts, while the Select were mostly steady, with continued light demand.

Most Choice round and loin cuts trended higher, especially tenderloins and the lighter short loin cuts, while the Select cuts struggled to trade at steady price levels most of the week. Closely trimmed items traded uneven again, Choice cuts were steady to firm and the Select were no more than steady.

Beef trimmings regained some of the losses suffered last week early in the trading week, but as the week progressed, some of the earlier gains were lost and by the end of the week beef trimmings were no more than steady to firm on light to moderate demand and offerings.
Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were generally weak on light demand and offerings.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 5.00 to 9.00 higher; Select and Choice chuck primal generally steady; Select and Choice round primal steady to 2.00 higher; Select and Choice loin primal 1.00 to 3.50 higher; Closely trimmed items steady to 2.00 higher; Beef trimmings 1.00 higher; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items generally 1.00 lower.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 2.40 at 110.00; 700/850 Up 2.88 at 107.76; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up .24 at 98.52; 700/850 Up 1.67 at 98.20.
